definitions.explanation: A variety of mandarin orange originally from India, now grown in Japan (especially Kyushu and Shikoku). Sweeter and more aromatic than common mandarins, with a slightly bumpy rind.

examples.japanese: ポンカン⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{甘|あま}くて→甘い：00617_amai⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Ponkans are sweet and have a nice fragrance.

examples.japanese: 1⟦{月|がつ}→月：30418_gatsu⟧⟦{頃|ごろ}→頃：00932_goro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ポンカン⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出回|でまわ}る→出回る：11736_demawaru⟧。

examples.english: My mother sent me a box of ponkans from Ehime.

notes:
Written in katakana even though the name comes from a place in India (Poona). Sold mainly in winter as a gift fruit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ポンカン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{剥|む}く→剥く：02305_muku⟧: to peel a ponkan
- {土佐|とさ}ポンカン: Tosa-grown ponkan (a famous regional variety)

- ⟦{温州|うんしゅう}みかん→温州みかん：28931_unshuumikan⟧: satsuma mandarin — milder, the most common Japanese variety
